about.title: Modesto Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product that fails should not become your problem to prove. In Modesto, as everywhere in California, product liability claims usually rest on strict liability: you show the item was defective in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and that the defect hurt you. Whether the maker was careless is generally beside the point. That rule matters for Stanislaus County residents dealing with a space heater that ignited, a ladder that buckled, a medication with a missing warning, or a vehicle part that gave way on Briggsmore Avenue or Coffee Road. Modesto recorded 1,365 injury collisions in 2025, and when a tire, airbag, or brake component plays a role, the claim can reach past the other driver to the company that built the part. Responsibility can extend along the whole chain, from manufacturer to distributor to the local retailer. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect you with an independent attorney who handles defective product cases on contingency, so nothing comes out of pocket unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Modesto Residents Start With LawProactive

items.title: Strict liability is on your side
items.desc: California generally does not require you to prove the manufacturer was negligent. An attorney in our network can focus on showing the design, manufacturing, or warning defect and how it caused your injury.

items.title: Every link in the chain can be accountable
items.desc: The manufacturer, the distributor, and the Modesto store that sold the item may each share responsibility. The right attorney knows how to identify all of them.

items.title: Preserving the product comes first
items.desc: The defective item itself is often the most important evidence. We connect you quickly so an attorney can advise on keeping it, its packaging, and receipts before anything is discarded or repaired.

items.question: I threw away the broken product after I was hurt in Modesto. Is my claim over?
items.answer: Not necessarily, but preserving the product is very important, so stop and keep whatever remains. Photos, receipts, packaging, the model number, and medical records can still help establish what happened. An attorney can also look into whether the same defect has affected other units.

items.question: Do I have to show the company knew the product was unsafe?
items.answer: Usually no. Under California's strict liability approach, the core questions are whether the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and whether that defect caused your injury. What the company knew or intended is generally not something you must prove.

items.question: My crash on Tully Road may have involved a faulty airbag. Who is responsible?
items.answer: It may be more than one party. The other driver could be responsible for the collision, while the airbag manufacturer, the automaker, or a parts distributor could be responsible for the defect that made your injuries worse. Keep the vehicle unrepaired if possible so an attorney can arrange an inspection.
